To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PGE systematics of mantle xenoliths in Ethiopian rift basalts reflect the effects of two successive episodes of melt percolation, with distinct geochemical signatures.

the PGE and Re–Os systematics of mantle xenoliths in Ethiopia are consistent with a heterogeneous lithospheric mantle, with variable degrees of depletion and metasomatism that reflect the distinct tectonomagnatic setting of the EARS.
the PGE and Re–Os signatures of mantle xenoliths provide insights on the processes and timing of lithosphere destruction beneath the East Africa Rift.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the mantle source regions for the magmatism in the Ethiopian segment of the East African rift.
the behavior of SCLM beneath the EARS and its transformation during rifting.
the transformation of continental lithospheres and the role that this plays in the global carbon and sulfur cycles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SCLM beneath the EARS has been modified by the arrival of the plumes and the subsequent extension, but the degree of transformation varies from place to place, with some regions being more advanced in the destruction process than others.
the SCLM beneath the EARS is heterogeneous and has been affected by multiple episodes of melt–rock interaction.

the PGE systematics in mantle xenolith from the East Africa Rift are consistent with the presence of two distinct mantle reservoirs: one with a depleted mantle signature (low PGE abundances and high 187Os/18Os ratios), and another with more enriched mantle signature (higher PGE abundances).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SCLM beneath the EARS is a heterogeneous assemblage of ancient lithospheric mantle, which was variably affected by the Afar and the Kenya plume.

the mantle xenoliths record the progressive transformation of the continental lithosphere beneath the Ethiopian rift, from a relatively depleted mantle with low Os isotopic ratios (Gundewyen), to a more depleted mantle with high Os isotopic ratios, and finally to an Os isotopic composition similar to the mantle plume (Dillo and Magedo).
the SCLM beneath the EARS has been subjected to two distinct processes: (1) early, low-volume, and oxidizing melt-percolation and (2) late-stage, high-volume, and reduced melt-percolation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mantle beneath the Ethiopian plateau is heterogeneous and has been affected by a variety of processes over time, with the most recent being the arrival of the plume and the onset of rifting, which led to the transformation of the SCLM.

the mantle beneath the EARS has undergone extensive refertilization, with variable timing and extent, during the last 65 Ma, with the most recent events associated with the arrival and melting of the Afar and/or Kenya plume.
the mantle xenoliths record a complex history of melt–rock interaction, with distinct processes and timing, which is likely to be common in other rift settings.
